comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C4-C7 regarding differential PPR between EPSCs and IPSCs. Both evaluations accept these findings as evidence for separate vesicle pools, with appropriate controls for ChR2 desensitization and axon vs terminal stimulation.
Perfect agreement on claims C8-C9 regarding differential Ca2+ sensitivity. Both evaluations accept this as strong evidence for distinct release properties supporting separate vesicle pools.

Perfect agreement on claims C10-C11 regarding Ca2+ channel pharmacology. Both accept the shared P/Q-type channel dependence and lack of N-type channel involvement, though this finding does not distinguish between vesicle pools.

Perfect agreement on claims C12-C13 regarding differential presynaptic modulation by DCG-IV and baclofen. Both evaluations accept this as evidence for distinct release properties between glutamate and GABA transmission.

Perfect agreement on claims C14-C16 regarding BAPTA/EGTA differential effects. Both evaluations treat this as key evidence for separate vesicle pools with different Ca2+ channel-vesicle coupling configurations.

Perfect agreement on claims C17-C21 regarding minimal stimulation experiments. Both accept these findings as evidence for independent release sites, with appropriate controls ruling out contamination between response types.
Perfect agreement on claim C22 regarding Sr2+ substitution experiments. Both accept this as complementary evidence supporting independent release from separate vesicle pools.

Perfect agreement on claims C29-C33 regarding differential short-term plasticity. Both evaluations accept the frequency-dependent depression of glutamate vs frequency-independent depression of GABA, with appropriate controls.
Perfect agreement on claims C34-C35 regarding pharmacological controls. Both accept these experiments as ruling out postsynaptic mechanisms and supporting presynaptic origin of plasticity.
Perfect agreement on claims C36-C39 regarding functional consequences of differential plasticity. Both accept these findings as demonstrating frequency-dependent modulation of granule cell firing.

Agreement on main conclusions C40-C41, though with nuanced differences. OpenEval finds the convergence of evidence strongly supports the conclusions. Peer reviewers also accept the conclusions but Reviewer 1 notes 'the strength of the conclusion rests on the abundance of data (approaches) rather than the decisiveness of any one approach.'

Partial overlap on anatomical characterization. OpenEval evaluates C1-C3 (viral injection, immunofluorescence, quantitative analysis), while peer review focuses on C2, C3, and C23 (EM evidence). Both accept the anatomical evidence as compelling.

Partial overlap on anatomical evidence. OpenEval evaluates C23-C26 (immunofluorescence, EM techniques, retrograde tracing), while peer review focuses on C24, C25, C27, C28 (EM and spatial segregation data). Both accept the evidence for segregated synapses from single terminals.

OpenEval evaluates C27-C28 (spatial segregation of postsynaptic sites) while peer review groups these with broader anatomical claims C24-C25. Both accept the evidence for segregated but proximal synapses.

OpenEval includes C26 (retrograde tracing ruling out VTA) as part of broader anatomical evidence R9, while peer review treats C26 separately as a control experiment. Both accept this finding without question.

OpenEval evaluates literature context claims C42-C48 regarding co-release in other brain regions and knowledge gaps. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically comment on literature framing.
OpenEval evaluates comparative context claims C49-C51 regarding differential release properties in other brain regions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates comparative context claims C52-C53 regarding P/Q-type channel dependence as general property of SuM neurons. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates biochemical evidence citations C54-C55 supporting vesicle segregation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates speculative functional implications C56-C58 as UNCERTAIN, noting they require additional validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically critique these speculative claims.
OpenEval evaluates integration claims C59-C60 connecting current findings with previous work on postsynaptic LTP. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates methodological claims C61-C65 regarding viral injection, slice preparation, and recording techniques. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not question the standard methods.
